segments.text: A cat sits in a pitch-dark yard at night.
Shine a flashlight, and its eyes flash bright.
But with zero light, they don't glow at all.
Light that enters passes through the retina.
A reflective layer bounces that light back.
The reflected light crosses the retina again.
That's what helps it see better in the dark.
Some of that light escapes back out of the eye.
That's the glow we actually see.
Without light to reflect, the eyes don't shine.
